newsitem.title: USA: Senate narrowly defeats Daschle abortion compromise.
newsitem.headline: Senate narrowly defeats Daschle abortion compromise.

text.p: The U.S. Senate Thursday evening defeated a measure drafted by Democratic leader Tom Daschle that aimed to restrict late-term abortions without specifically banning the controversial procedure known as "partial birth" abortions earlier in pregnancy.

The vote, 64-36, paves the way for the Senate to take up the bill sponsored by Pennsylvania Republican Rick Santorum which would prohibit the procedure -- known as partial birth abortion or dilation and extraction -- at any time in a pregnancy, except to save a woman's life. That vote is likely to take place early next week.
President Clinton has vowed to veto the Santorum bill because it does not make exceptions for the health of a pregnant woman.

The Daschle alternative would have limited all late-term abortions, through partial birth or four other surgical procedures, except in cases where the pregnant woman faced what Daschle called "extraordinary" health risks. A similar measure sponsored by California Democrat Dianne Feinstein, with a broader health exemption, was defeated by 72-28 vote earlier Thursday.

Daschle and his backers, including some moderate Republicans, tried to frame the measure as an alternative that could be embraced by senators on both sides of the abortion divide. Daschle said it protected fetuses from all surgical abortions after "viability," when they could survive outside the womb, without trodding on the constitutionally protected right to abortion earlier in pregnancy.
Santorum and other critics said the health exemption was too broad, and that the bill would not stop a single abortion.
